verses.1: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the elect of God and the knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
verses.2: in hope of eternal life, which the trustworthy God promised long ago before the ages,
verses.3: has now made it plain in his own times through the preaching of his word, which I was entrusted with in accordance with the command of our Savior God,
verses.4: to Titus, my true son in the shared faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus the Savior of us.
verses.5: For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you might put what is lacking into order, and appoint elders in every city, just as I instructed you,
verses.6: if someone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having believing children who are not accused of indulgence or rebellion.
verses.7: For the overseer must be blameless as a steward of God, not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not a heavy drinker, not a brawler, not greedy for gain,
verses.8: but hospitable, a lover of good, sensible, upright, holy, self-controlled,
verses.9: holding fast to the faithful word as taught, so that he may be able both to encourage with sound teaching and to refute those who contradict it.
verses.10: For there are many who are rebellious, empty talkers, and deluders, especially those from the circumcision,
verses.11: whom it is necessary to silence, for they overturn whole households by teaching what should not be done for the sake of shameful gain.
verses.12: One of their own prophets said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies."
verses.13: This testimony is true. For this reason rebuke them sharply, so that they may be healthy in the faith,
verses.14: not paying attention to Jewish myths and commandments that turn away from the truth, given by men.
verses.15: To those who are pure, all things are pure; but to those who are defiled and without faith, nothing is pure, for both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
verses.16: They profess to know God, but by their works they deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "the elect of God" reflects the term "ἐκλεκτῶν θεοῦ" as a genitive absolute, indicating the scope of the apostleship.
- v. 14: "Jewish myths" is a rendering of "Ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοις," which could also be read as "Judaizing myths" or "Jewish fables," but the former is clearer in context.
- v. 15: "To those who are pure" and "To those who are defiled" render "πάντα καθαρὰ τοῖς καθαροῖς· τοῖς δὲ μεμιαμμένοις" with clarity, preserving the contrast.
